The annotated candidate has been saved to answer.json.

The solution adds a single `/*@ */` loop annotation block before the `while` loop with:
- `loop invariant -10 <= x - y <= 10;` — since each iteration adds 10 to both `x` and `y`, their difference is loop-invariant, and the requires (`0 <= x,y <= 10`) bounds it at entry.
- `loop assigns x, y;` — the only variables modified in the loop.

No `loop variant` was emitted because `while (unknown())` has unprovable/unknown termination, and omitting it avoids an unprovable termination goal. After the loop, `x - y` stays in `[-10, 10]`, so when `y == 0` we have `x = x - y ∈ [-10, 10]`, proving the original `assert(x != 20)`.

All original C tokens, the original `requires` contract, and the original `//@ assert(x != 20)` are preserved verbatim.
